text:
leo: noticed another onboarding footgun: generator ergonomics in Go feel inconsistent w.r.t cancellation. users expect that cancelling the supplied ctx always tears everything down. currently some internal retries/auth goroutines survive.

anya: can you share a tiny repro? curious if this is the same class as the other ctx-shim issues.

leo: simplified repro below: create generator with parent ctx, immediately cancel after starting consumer goroutine. sometimes the consumer goroutine blocks in the decoder read during handshake and process doesn't exit.

leo: root cause in my investigation: our auth retry helper spawns a background goroutine that uses a derived context instead of inheriting the caller's ctx. that goroutine may hold a reference to transport/response and prevent stream closure.

pradeep: solution idea: two parts: (1) align to errgroup.WithContext so all spawned helpers inherit parent cancellation; (2) expose a Generator.Close() that cancels internal resources and is documented as the explicit way to stop streaming.

anya: exposing Close() is good for explicit cleanup, but we must keep ctx-cancel-first semantics: cancelling the passed ctx should be equivalent to Close(). If we add Close(), make it call cancel on internal ctx and be idempotent.

leo: agreed. implementation notes: store a cancel func on generator struct created as ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(parent); then use errgroup.WithContext(ctx) for retries/refresh loops so they stop when either cancel() or parent is cancelled. Close() calls cancel().

pradeep: also add defensive req = req.WithContext(ctx) right before RoundTrip. Middleware refactors sometimes replaced request context earlier in the chain and that bit ensures transport honors cancellation.

anya: tests: add a tiny integration in sampleapp that starts generator, cancels immediately and asserts process exits within 200ms. Avoid flaky NumGoroutine assertions; rely on process exit timing in e2e.

leo: created branch gen-api-close-errgroup with the changes and a short README note about calling Close() or cancelling ctx. CI triggered.

ci-bot: CI queued for gen-api-close-errgroup (build #4501).

pradeep: quick follow-up: audit other places we use ctxshims and retry loops (upload, embeddings client) for similar patterns. I'll open a tracking issue.

anya: aesthetic: add godoc note on Generator.Close() and a short example in SDK README showing idiomatic use (defer gen.Close() right after creating generator).

leo: thanks folks. hoping this reduces onboarding confusion — had a new user file a bug "sample app never exits" yesterday.
